**Lloyd Dane** (August 19, 1925 – December 11, 2015) was an American [NASCAR Grand National Series] driver from [Eldon, Missouri].[[1]] He participated part-time in the 1951 and 1954 to 1964 seasons, capturing four wins, all in his own car.[[1]] Two of Dane's wins came during the [1956 season], when he finished 23rd in points.[[1]]

Dane first started racing in 1949 and was the first [NASCAR Pacific Coast Late Model Series] champion; he took the championship in [1954], 1956 and 1957.[[2]] He was noted for driving a [Hudson Hornet], which he drove to his 1954 championship, along with longtime friend [Tim Flock].

**Eldon** is a city in [Miller County], [Missouri], United States, located 30 miles (48 km) southwest of [Jefferson City]. The population was 4,416 as of the [2020 census].[[3]]

## History

[[edit]]

Eldon was [platted] in 1881, and according to tradition, named after a railroad official.[[5]] The railroad closed down in 1980 and is proposed to be transformed into the extension of the [Rock Island Trail] "Rock Island Trail State Park (Missouri)"). A post office called Eldon has been in operation since 1881.[[6]]

### 2019 tornado

[[edit]]

Main article: [Tornado outbreak of May 20–23, 2019]

On the night of May 22, 2019, a tornado touched down west of Eldon. It came through Eldon damaging many homes and businesses. The same tornado struck [Jefferson City] later in the evening.[[7]]

## Geography

[[edit]]

Eldon is in northwestern Miller County. The city is served by [U.S. Route 54] and Missouri Routes [52] and [87]. [Jefferson City] is 30 miles (48 km) to the northeast, while the city of [Lake Ozark] is 12 miles (19 km) to the south. [Bagnell Dam], which forms the [Lake of the Ozarks], is 11 miles (18 km) south of Eldon.[[8]]

According to the [U.S. Census Bureau], the city of Eldon has a total area of 3.56 square miles (9.22 km 2), all land.[[1]] The city sits on high ground: the northwest side of the city drains toward [South Moreau Creek], part of the [Moreau River] "Moreau River (Missouri)") watershed flowing to the [Missouri River], while the northeast side of the city is the source of Blythes Creek, a tributary of South Moreau Creek. The southeast side of Eldon drains into Saline Creek, a tributary of the [Osage River], which in turn flows northeastern to the Missouri River.
